scope: Fresh review of all 40 assigned videos. I read each full narration script, viewed every scene storyboard and motion.png, inspected at least one native encoded frame, and visually reviewed motion-all-scenes.png with early, middle, and late encoded samples for the highest-motion narration beat in every scene. Scores independently rate explanatory visuals and meaningful causal animation. A lesson is ready only when both scores are at least 90 and no medium/high issue remains. These samples do not establish continuous playback, full audible listening, or every-frame review.

findings.issue: Several architecture terms and shape labels compete in the compact KV-memory view, weakening the otherwise useful comparison.
findings.fix: Reveal cache dimensions and retained-token growth in separate steps, keeping the active sequence axis and unit visible.

findings.issue: The current encoded fit scene begins at the fitted parameters and holds near-identical line states, so it skips the gradient descent that should connect the stated starting line to the least-squares fit.
findings.fix: Derive each parameter update, prediction line, and loss from the same dataset. Animate the line through successive gradient steps, show the matching loss decrease, and hold the final state before the next scene.

findings.issue: The capacity and generalization panels are largely static, so the relationship between added hypothesis choices and weaker holdout confidence stays abstract.
findings.fix: Keep one predictor and sample set visible while expanding the hypothesis set, then carry the resulting fit to the untouched holdout points.

findings.issue: The contract-change sequence explains point-in-time leakage and preprocessing parity, but the transform is mostly presented as a set of states.
findings.fix: Animate training-only fit statistics once, then reuse that frozen transform across validation and serving rows to show where parity breaks.

findings.issue: The audit and oversight panels carry many labels at once; the viewer has to scan a dense evidence dashboard instead of following the changing decision trail.
findings.fix: Keep one case selected and reveal evidence, owner, review outcome and retained record in causal order, with inactive rows muted.

findings.issue: Similarity moves meaningfully, but permission, freshness and answer-version checks read mostly as fixed gates.
findings.fix: Reuse one candidate answer and animate it through separate permission and freshness outcomes, retaining the reason each rejected candidate cannot be served.

findings.issue: Most scenes hold query and evidence diagrams as finished panels. The lesson explains how expansion and decomposition change the search, but only ranked-list fusion visibly accumulates much state.
findings.fix: Animate one natural-language query splitting into independent subquestions, retrieve evidence for each, then recombine results while keeping the original access scope and provenance attached.

findings.issue: The check sequence and latency budget stay almost fixed while the narration explains how safety checks affect an allowed action. Viewers do not see a request travel through the checks or watch their cost accumulate.
findings.fix: Carry one request through the actual check order, show each result and elapsed time, then let the authorization decision determine whether the effect proceeds.

findings.issue: The proposed action and permission boundary appear as a static panel, so the critical transition from a valid-looking proposal to authorized execution remains abstract.
findings.fix: Carry one concrete tool action through scope validation, policy check, approval, and execution. Show the blocked branch when a required permission is absent.

findings.issue: The query tile and key/value blocks remain nearly static while the narration explains streaming and reuse; the memory-saving loop is not visible until the later rescale example.
findings.fix: Animate successive key/value tiles passing one resident query tile, updating the running maximum and partial sums, then show the final normalized output.

findings.issue: The before/after matrix makes the regression count inspectable, but its mostly fixed layout asks the viewer to read four cells rather than watch the evidence accumulate.
findings.fix: Animate each query outcome into the paired matrix while keeping the baseline/candidate identity fixed, then call attention to the eight regressions before showing the net gain.

findings.issue: The run, data, prompt, and logged model identities are shown as a mostly fixed graph. The lesson explains lineage questions without visibly reconstructing one run from those linked records; the synthesis scene carries most of the changing review state.
findings.fix: Select one run, attach its exact code/data/prompt identities in sequence, then carry that model identity into the downstream request trace so the reconstruction path stays explicit.

findings.issue: The FP16 cancellation example is displayed as a precomputed before/after comparison. The intermediate cast and rounding step that erases the small term are not animated, leaving the core numerical mechanism hard to see.
findings.fix: Animate 256 + 1 through the FP16 cast, show it rounding back to 256, then subtract 256. Keep the FP32 accumulator beside it so the two results can be compared at each operation.
